_comment: The API Product for solution 06. POST to /api/orgs/<ORG_ID>/products, then deploy per environment with POST /api/orgs/<ORG_ID>/envs/<ENV_ID>/products/<PRODUCT_ID>/deploy. apiIds come from GET /api/orgs/<ORG_ID>/apis. Or just ask the Agent — see ../helix-agent-prompt.md.
_why_a_product_exists_here: This solution is about signing, not about selling. The product is here because it is the only way to get a CREDENTIAL: an app subscribes to a product, and creating the app is what mints the key_id and secret_key the caller signs with. No product, no app; no app, no credential; no credential, nothing to sign with.
_authMethods_is_the_field_that_matters: authMethods MUST list hmac-auth. It defaults to ["helix-auth"], and an app created under a product that does not name hmac-auth is rejected. This is the single most likely thing to get wrong when adapting solution 02's or 03's products file.
_the_credential: Create the app with plugins: {"hmac-auth": {}} — an EMPTY config object. The control plane generates key_id and secret_key and returns them ONCE, in the create response. Supply your own values there instead if you must match a secret a partner already holds. Rotating regenerates both; there is no way to rotate one and keep the other.
_quota_is_mandatory: Every product MUST carry a quota object; a product with no quota is rejected at creation. Note that the quota is only ENFORCED if api-product-enforcer is on the route, which this solution does not put there — see solution 01 for metering, and this package's README for what is and isn't known about combining it with hmac-auth.

products.name: partner-events
products.description: Signed access to the Partner Events API. One app per partner integration, each with its own key_id and secret_key, so a compromised secret is rotated for one partner rather than all of them.
